contributions.statement: When one agent task carries several spec targets, give every target its own acceptance test and fail the change if any target has none, because silently skipped or half-done targets ('Missing Implementation') were about 29% of even the strongest model's failures.
contributions.evidence: §5.6 Fig. 9, App. H Fig. 15: failure classification across 13 models on 115 multi-target tasks (median 5 targets, ~51 files); Claude-Opus-4.7 profile: 55% implementation error, 29% missing implementation, 4% build error. Classifier validated per review; single trials.
relative_to: 2607.17937 silent dropped obligations under long context

contributions.statement: A compile/build gate catches much of a weaker model's failures (build errors 28-41%) but almost none of a frontier model's (4-15%), so with frontier models the behavioral tests carry the whole verification load.
contributions.evidence: §5.6 and App. H per-model profiles (Seed-2.0-Pro 41% build error vs Opus 4% / DeepSeek 15%). No Java; uneven reasoning-effort settings across models.

reason: Beyond the leaderboard, the per-tier failure analysis says what a gate must check for multi-target spec work. The headline resolve rates alone would add nothing over other long-horizon benchmarks.
